seo.title: Cairnly for employers | Career clarity your people own
seo.description: Give your people a clear answer about where their skills fit, inside or outside your company. Per-head pricing, one afternoon to roll out, and you never see an individual result.

hero.title: Give your people career path clarity. Even if it's not with you.
hero.body: One assessment and one conversation with an AI career coach, and within an hour someone has ten named roles that fit their skills, personality and goals, each with a match score, salary data and an AI-impact rating. Employees own the result. You pay per head, roll it out with a batch of codes, and never see who took it or what came out.

why.lead: Most people have no idea whether the role they're in still fits the person they've become. They stay because it's easier than finding out.
why.p1: The numbers say the same thing. Gallup has 14% of Dutch employees engaged at work, and 86% saying it's a good time to find a job where they live. That's not loyalty. That's a workforce waiting for a reason. Only 15% of employees say their manager helped them build a career plan in the last six months, so the conversation that would settle it isn't happening either.
why.p2: Cairnly gives them the answer in one sitting. Some will find their best next step is inside your company, in a role you hadn't thought to offer. Some will find it's elsewhere, and leave on good terms with a plan. Either way you get honest conversations instead of guesswork, and you get them before anything turns into a file.

how.title: Three steps, all of them the employee's

steps.title: The assessment
steps.body: The employee uploads their CV and answers the assessment, about half an hour. Cairnly's workflows, built with working career coaches on top of Schein's Career Anchors and Big Five research, produce a first analysis.

steps.title: The conversation
steps.body: An AI career coach walks them through ten roles across four categories: the closest fits, the stretch options, the adjacent moves, and one wild card. Picked from thousands of real job titles, not a category list. They push back where it's wrong, and the report is rewritten before it's final.

steps.title: The next move
steps.body: The final report, plus the tools to act on it: live openings per role, and a CV and cover letter tailored to each application (in beta). Whether they look inside or outside your company is up to them.

employeeSees.intro: The first screen of a company-sponsored assessment says this, word for word:
employeeSees.quote: Your employer paid for this. They will never see your answers, your scores or your report. Nobody at your company will know whether you finished it.
employeeSees.why: That line is there because an assessment people suspect is being read by HR is an assessment people answer strategically. Then it's worthless to everyone.

council.eyebrow: Built to pass your works council
council.intro: Three things make this an easy yes for an OR, a staff council or a union rep:

items.title: Voluntary.
items.body: Nobody is required to take it and nobody is asked why they didn't.

items.title: Offered to a group.
items.body: A team, a department or the whole company. Never to one person.

items.title: The employer sees nothing.
items.body: Not the roles, not the scores, not who redeemed a code. You see a count, and that's it.

items.title: A batch of codes, and a count
items.body: Codes for the number of people you want to cover. Hand them out however you like: HR email, intranet, a manager in a team meeting. Afterwards you see how many were redeemed. Nothing else. Or skip the codes and let people buy it themselves and expense it. Batches are cheaper.

items.title: A rollout kit
items.body: An announcement email for employees, a paragraph for your intranet, and a one-page note for your works council, all written so the tool is framed the way it should be. Takes you fifteen minutes, not an afternoon.

items.title: Aggregated feedback, from 20 employees up
items.body: Below that number we don't report anything, because below that number someone could be picked out of the aggregate.

items.title: Employability budgets
items.body: Employability and development budgets, especially where a collective agreement or sector fund expects you to offer career orientation.

items.title: Reorganisations
items.body: Reorganisations and voluntary leave schemes, as the first step before someone decides whether they need full outplacement.

items.title: After a merger
items.body: Onboarding after a merger, when nobody is quite sure which roles still make sense.

items.title: Development conversations
items.body: Annual development conversations, as something concrete to talk about instead of a generic growth plan.

fits.uk: Preparing for the Employment Rights Act? From January 2027 unfair dismissal protection starts at six months and the compensation cap goes. A voluntary career tool is the least contentious thing you can put in front of people before then.

about.p1: Cairnly is built by Human in the Loop B.V. in Utrecht, the Netherlands. My wife and I started it after sitting with the "is this still the right job" question ourselves and finding nothing that gave a straight answer. Career coaches use it as the opening step of their own programmes. Employers use it to give people the same starting point without the programme.
about.p2Before: How the method works is public at
about.p2After: . If you want to talk, email us or book 20 minutes.

items.q: Can we see who took it?
items.a: No. You see how many codes were redeemed, not by whom. If you need names, this isn't the right tool.

items.q: Can we target it at specific people?
items.a: You can, but don't. Offer it to a team, a department or everyone. A career tool handed to one person by their manager reads as a message, and everyone will read it that way, including your works council.

items.q: Does this replace outplacement or coaching?
items.a: No. It's the cheap step in front of them. People arrive at the expensive part already knowing what they're looking for.

It's built on Career Anchors and Big Five research and reviewed by working career coaches. It is not a certified psychometric instrument and we don't claim it is. Where Anchors gives you a preference, Cairnly gives you named roles, salary and AI exposure for each. The method is public.
Employee data sits with Cairnly, not with you. We never share individual results with an employer. GDPR applies and we'll sign a processing agreement if your DPO asks.

items.q: Do we need to involve our works council?
items.a: A voluntary, group-wide development tool where the employer sees no results usually doesn't need formal consent, but check with them anyway. Our one-page note is written for exactly that conversation.

items.q: What if someone takes it and leaves?
items.a: Then they were going to leave anyway, and now they leave with a plan and on good terms. The ones who stay, stay for a reason. Resume Now's 2025 survey found 58% of workers regret staying at a job too long and 38% regret quitting one. Staying too long is the more common mistake.
